question.leadin: This ruler's most famous victory came at the Battle of Hattin.
question.text: Name this Kurdish ruler who founded the Ayyubid dynasty. He reconquered Jerusalem for the Islamic world in 1187.
question.answerHtml: Saladin [or Ṣalāḥ ad-Dīn, or Selahedîn, or Yusuf ibn Ayyub ibn Shadi]
question.clue: This ruler was defeated at the Battle of Arsuf by his rival during a larger conflict in which that rival was able to retake control of Joffa.

swap.leadin: Albert Einstein turned down the presidency of this country.
swap.text: Identify this country that declared independence in 1948 following the end of British rule in Mandatory Palestine. It is the only officially Jewish country in the world.
swap.clue: This country's early "Austerity" period led it to sign a reparations agreement with West Germany under its first leader David Ben-Gurion.

question.leadin: Name the following Middle Eastern countries.
question.text: This country's city of Madaba is known for its Byzantine map depicting the Holy Land. The city of Aqaba is also in this "Hashemite Kingdom."
question.clue: Leila Khaled and the Sandinista Patrick Arguello were captured while trying to hijack a plane and take it to the Dawson's Field landing strip in this country which formed the Arab Federation with a western neighbour.

swap.text: A second oil shock occurred in 1979, partially due to this country's regime change and a subsequent war with Iraq. Shah Mohammed Reza Pahlavi was deposed as leader of this country by the Ayatollah Khomeini.
swap.clue: This country was led by Mohammad Mosaddegh, and this nation's Qajar dynasty was replaced by its Pahlavi dynasty.

question.text: The early Muslims were overwhelmingly of this ethnicity, namesake of the peninsula from whence they came. An approximate meaning derived from regional cognates is something like nomad or passerby.
question.clue: These people fought on both sides of the Battle of Badr and conquered the Sassanid Empire.

swap.leadin: The Mamluks constructed a series of warehouses called khans along the road from this city to the "breadbasket" region of Hauran.
swap.text: Name this city which was the seat of the Umayyad Caliphate. This city names a rare style of flowing steel.
swap.clue: This city was home to the Hanbali jurist Ibn Taymiyyah, and it is the site of the mausoleums of the two most prominent leaders of the Zengid Dynasty, Nur al-Din and Saladin, who both died in this city.

question.leadin: Sometimes leaving no choice but going through your enemies leads to victory.
question.text: Tariq ibn Ziyad captured Hispania for this Islamic caliphate after forcing his soldiers to burn their ships.
question.clue: This empire began following the First Fitna, led by Muawiyah I. Its expansion was halted in 732 CE, following Abd al-Rahman's defeat at the Battle of Tours.

swap.leadin: Name these largest cities of their respective Asian nations that are NOT capital cities.
swap.text: One of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world, it flourished in the past due to its location at the end of the Silk Road. Many Armenian Christians have sought refuge here due to its position in northeastern Syria.
swap.clue: A rebuilt version of the Ayyubid Palace of Glory is contained within a defensive structure used by Seleucus Nicator, this massive Citadel of this city, outside of which Tamerlane built a tower of 20,000 skulls after taking it from the Mamluks.

question.leadin: Jerusalem's Old City is home to a quarter named for this country, the first officially Christian nation in the world.
question.text: Name this modern-day country whose diaspora communities grew after its people were targeted for extermination by the Ottoman Empire in 1915.
question.clue: A ruler of this kingdom abandoned the worship of deities like Anahit in favor of Christianity to curb Sassanian influence and built the world's oldest cathedral in Etchmiadzin .

swap.leadin: These people founded the Sultanate of Rum over what had been Byzantine Anatolia.
swap.text: Name this Turkish dynasty which branched off from the Oghuz Turks. It was a major power in the Near and Middle East from its 11th-century victory at Manzikert into the early 14th century.
swap.clue: One offshoot of this dynastic group was the Sultanate of Rum.

question.leadin: Name these sacred cities from various world religions.
question.text: This Arab city derives its holiness from being the destination of Mohammed's Hejirah, the journey he made after being driven out of Mecca.
question.clue: A violation of a pact with this city's leaders led to the execution of the Jewish tribe of Qurayza .

swap.text: Ahmad Sanjar, a later Seljuk Turk ruler, fought campaigns against these Ismaili Muslims whose name now describes their common action of covertly killing rulers they didn't like.

question.leadin: This leader invited 400 beys to the Cairo Citadel to celebrate the endowment of military command to his son Tusun, only to slaughter them.
question.text: Name this commander who ended over 500 years of Mamluk dominance of Egypt, eventually seizing the title of Wali for himself. His dynasty would rule Egypt until they were overthrown by the Free Officers Movement.
question.answerHtml: Muhammad Ali Pasha [prompt on Pasha alone; reject “Muhammad” or “Ali” alone]
question.clue: A fleet led by this leader's son lost a battle against Admiral Edward Codrington that led to Greek independence.

swap.leadin: During a battle, a general of these people flung off his helmet and yelled "oh my Islam" to prevent the enemy escaping from one side of the battle.
swap.text: Name this state, whose ruler Qutuz was assassinated shortly after winning a battle against a seemingly unstoppable Ilkhanate in 1260.

question.text: After Gemayel's assassination, the IDF gave Phalangist militias access to a refugee camp and a Shia neighborhood in Beirut, resulting in this massacre that forced Ariel Sharon ("sha-ROHN") to resign as defense minister.
question.clue: Elie Hobeika's forces were able to carry on slaughtering people through the night thanks to flares fired from a third party, which led the Kahan Commission to declare the sitting Defense Minister "personally responsible."

swap.leadin: Abd al-Rahman ibn Muljam, a member of this sect of Islam, plotted to kill Mu'awiyya, 'Amr ibn-al-'As, and another leader all on the same day with a poisoned saber. He only succeeded once.
swap.text: The aforementioned dude was a member of this sect, whose name comes from their withdrawal from mainstream Islam after a certain dude hero-worshipped in Iran agreed to arbitration with Mu'awiyya.
swap.clue: Once selected as Caliph, Ali faced several revolts during the First Fitna, including by this breakaway sect which Ali defeated at the Battle of Nahrawan.

question.text: The first Umayyad, Abu Sufyan, was a member of this tribe, which controlled Mecca during the time of Muhammad. Divisions of this tribe included the Banu Hashim.
question.answerHtml: Quraysh [or Kuraish or Koreish or Quresh or Qurrish or Qurish or Qirsh or Qureshi or Coreish]
question.clue: Muhammad's Hashemites were one of 10 clans in this ruling tribe of Mecca. The Umayyads and Rashiduns traced their lineage to other clans in this group of peoples.

swap.text: The most upwardly mobile Persians belonged to this family, who had originally been Buddhist administrators in the Balkh region. The use of this family's name to describe an imaginary feast may relate from an anti-Persian attack on their false hospitality.
swap.clue: Harun also destroyed the power of this family after one of its members impregnated his sister Abassa. This family patronized scholars such as Geber and was influential during the early years of the caliphate.

question.text: The Kurdish genocide was codenamed the "campaign" of this eighth sura of the Quran, whose English translation is roughly "the spoils of war."

swap.text: Meanwhile, this agreement to divide the Middle East into British and French spheres of influence was undermining the promises made to Husayn.
swap.clue: In this agreement, Tsarist Russia claimed Istanbul and one signatory gained control over Acre, Haifa, Jordan, and Iraq.
